title: decide tour: a new home screen for a task app
intro:
A sample round that shows every feature. Pick with a click or the digits **1–9**, **J / K** move between questions, **?** lists all shortcuts.

If a question is unclear, press **E** or the button under it. When the agent is online it answers right under the question; otherwise it explains in the next round. Questions you leave open get the agent's recommendation.
context: Right now the app opens on one long list with every task. An active user has about 140 of them, and the ones due today get lost among the rest. We read the last 50 messages in the feedback form: 31 of them are about a missed deadline.

glossary.feature flag: A switch inside the app: only the people it's turned on for see the new feature. It can be turned off in a second, without a new release.
glossary.PR: Pull request: a proposal to add code to the shared branch. It gets reviewed before it's merged.
glossary.migration: A script that changes the database once, for every existing record.

questions.title: What matters most in the first version of the home screen?
questions.tldr: This decides what we build first and what waits.
questions.what: We pick one main goal for the release.
questions.why: One week of design isn't enough for everything at once.
questions.how: The other goals aren't dropped; they go into the next PR.
questions.goal: A clear test of success we can check with real users.

options.label: People see what's due
options.detail: Overdue and today's tasks on top, everything else below.
options.recommended: 31 of the last 50 complaints are about a missed deadline; it's the main pain.
pros: Easy to measure: missed deadlines per week
cons: Works best when tasks have due dates

options.label: The app opens instantly
options.detail: Speed work without changing the look.
pros: Fewer drop-offs on a bad connection

questions.title: Which home screen layout do we go with?
questions.tldr: Three mockups. Click a picture to look closer.

options.label: One list
options.detail: Everything in one scrollable list, like now but tidier.

options.label: Today view
options.detail: Overdue and today's tasks on top, the rest folded under Later.
options.recommended: Puts what's due first and keeps everything else one tap away.
pros: What's due is the first thing you see
cons: Tasks without a date sit in Later

options.label: Board by status
options.detail: Columns by status; drag a card to move it.
pros: Good overview of work in progress
cons: Sorted by status, not by date

options.label: Reminders

options.label: Recurring tasks

questions.title: In what order do we build it?
questions.tldr: Drag, or use the arrows. Top goes first.

questions.title: How sure are you that people plan by day rather than by project?
How do we roll it out?
questions.tldr: Speed against the risk of breaking the app for people who open it every morning.
questions.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A[Ready] --> B{Roll out how}
  B -->|at once| C[All users]
  B -->|gradually| D[10% of users] --> E[All users]
  B -->|flag| F[Our team only]

options.label: Everyone at once
cons: If it breaks, it breaks for everyone at once

options.label: Gradually
options.recommended: A bug shows up for a small share of users, not all of them.

options.label: Behind a feature flag
options.detail: Turned on by hand for specific accounts.
cons: Someone has to remember to turn it on

questions.title: What share of users do we start with?
questions.tldr: This question appeared because you picked a gradual rollout.

options.recommended: Enough to catch bugs, and it affects few people.

questions.title: What do we do with old tasks that have no due date?
questions.tldr: A migration that can't be undone: afterwards we can't tell which dates were real.

code.text:
-- gives every old task a due date
UPDATE task
   SET due_at = created_at
 WHERE due_at IS NULL;

options.label: Use the creation date
options.detail: Each old task gets the day it was created.
cons: Old forgotten tasks show up as overdue

options.label: A separate "No date" section
options.detail: We leave them as they are.
options.recommended: Guessing would fill Overdue with tasks nobody meant to date, and it can't be undone.
cons: The section may end up big
